title: Thinking Recursively (Part 2): Updating a Tuple in a List & Dual Accumulators
solutionExplanation: Implements tail-recursive list updates and dual-accumulator partitioning with O(1) stack space.

otpDocCards.complexityNote: Processes stream in O(N) time with minimal heap garbage.

mentalModelCheck.question: When updating a single tuple in an immutable list using tail recursion, why must you continue recursing on Rest after finding the match?

options.label: To accumulate the remaining elements of the list so they are preserved in the final reversed list
options.explanation: Stopping immediately would drop all elements that appeared after the target item in the original list.

options.label: Because the BEAM bytecode verifier requires every function to process at least 1,000 items
options.explanation: Erlang has no arbitrary item threshold; lists of any length are supported.

options.label: To check if the TargetId exists multiple times in the global atom table
options.explanation: Product IDs are integers, not atoms.
